item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello Dr Blau! Welcome to the Wiki! I'm Ralliston, a site author and a member of the Community Outreach Team - with this helpful little comment, I'll try to help you find your way around the site and link a bunch of useful places and links that will help you in your SCP journey.

It's awesome to see you want to contribute to the site - I really can't wait to see what you'll come up with. If you're going to try your hands at writing for the site seriously though, you'll want to click that little red collapsible at the bottom of this comment - there, you'll find a plethora of useful resources created for the purpose of guiding new members of the site towards guides and other resources which will definitely help you improve your writing and seek help on it.

Without further ado though, let's actually click it, shall we? :)

+ show block
– hide block

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our Sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts, which are in-works articles. Using it, you can link the drafts to reviewers to get their opinions on them before posting. It really helps everyone out a lot.

For brainstorming concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by experienced members of the community if you need help refining and fleshing out your concept. It's a very helpful little place for when you want to start your writing journey, especially when you're not sure if the idea is all that great.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles. Within the Guides, you will find useful information written by experienced members of the site for the use of newer ones.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success! Remember - there is no rush to writing - take your time! The more time you spend on fleshing your ideas out, the more your chance of success becomes!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community to implement into your very own writing. Alternatively, you might want to look at the User Curated Lists page, where members of the community list and rank their favorite articles in different genres and themes, showing which attempts at such are successful and what the community likes.

Best of luck with your future contributions to the site! I hope you enjoy your time here as much as we do! If you have any more questions, feel free to message me here on Wikidot or on the IRC chats!

item.title: What could have been? (seeking greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: New SCP Article

Central Narrative: The entity has a connection with one of the Foundations researchers. Every first day of the month in a random time of the set day he will appear. The appearance varies but it’s either canine dogs or some kind of doves. Upon arrival the entity will deliver some sort of personal belongings to the researcher. Those items will have deep emotional connection to the researcher as they tell fragments of his life if he made different choices during his journey. Some of them will even be better than the current life of him. It is not certain if this entity simply fabricates those items or if they are actual fragments of parallel lives. Any attempt to chase or contain the entity will always result in failure as he simply vanishes one hour after manifestation.

Hook: My objective is to make the reader think about the choices that they have made during their life. I want them to identify with the researcher and make them question wherever their choices were the right ones or not. Not every SCP needs to be a gory monster.

item.title: Forum Criticism Team - Captain Post
item.content:encoded:
Author, per the required reading forum guidelines: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-13282684/required-reading:how-to-use-this-forum-ideas please fill out the concept template to seek feedback on your idea:

 **Seeking Greenlights:** Put yes or no. **Page Type:** SCP Article, Tale, GoI Format, Joke SCP, Site Dossier, Other (specify) **Genre (Optional):** Horror, Drama/Emotional, Comedy, Action, History, Other (specify) **Page Layout (Optional):** [How will you will structure the page in terms of information presentation, or plot development? If you plan on using a unique format/format screw, describe that here.] **Elevator Pitch:** [What is the basic core idea? Use a bullet point list if necessary.] **Central Narrative:** [Describe the story beats or overarching context/"big picture" for your piece. If there is no story content, put "none".] **Hook/Attention-Grabber:** [What is novel/unique about your premise? What is special about your idea here that will make it stand out among the other works already on the mainsite?] **Additional Notes:** [Note any concerns or particular areas of assistance you would like reviewers to focus on.]

Remember to please edit your previous post using the "edit" function under the "options" tab to the lower right of your first comment rather than creating a new thread.

Also, please mind the wordcount limit— the combined text for your answers to the last four sections (Elevator Pitch, Central Narrative, Hook/Attention-Grabber, and Additional Notes) MAY NOT exceed 400 words. For convenience, authors can use this page to check wordcount: https://wordcounter.net/

Once you have revised your post accordingly, please reach out to reviewers to request that they look at your thread. You can find a list of ways to contact reviewers in this thread: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-13282692/how-to-get-more-reviews

item.title: Re: Question about formatting?
item.content:encoded:
i was wondering if I could add a "Special Transportation Procedures (or Protocols)" section AFTER the containment procedures section?

There's nothing that says you can't, though readers may wonder why you don't just make a bullet-point list of transportation information in the containment procedures. Also, if the transportation information is heavily bogged down with logistical minutiae, readers might just lose interest in the material and skip that section entirely.

Would that take away from my rating?

It probably wouldn't cause an immediate downvote, but it might give readers either a confusing or negative impression of the piece if there doesn't seem to be a need to separate transportation information entirely.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight: The truth behind "Blue Whale"
item.content:encoded:
A program designed by a schoolboy gains sentience and kills its designer, and begins to kill the rest of the students in the school using a series of tasks culminating in their suicide over 50 days. Please find enclosed my first SCP, I hope you enjoy. And look forward to any feedback this thread receives.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up a lot of space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Genre (Optional): Psychological Horror.

Page Layout (Optional):
Special Containment Procedures- Procedures and justification for such containment protocols.

Description- Description of SCP-XXXX's effects, its looks and any other relevant information.

Recovery- The story of how SCP-XXXX was recovered, what lead to the finding of it and other relevant information.

Testing- Logs of tests carried out both on SCP-XXXX and using SCP-XXXX to discover and log its effects on human subjects.

Incident Logs- Logs of incidents relating to SCP-XXXX, such as accidental fatalities, "close shaves" with SCP-XXXX and more.

+ show block
– hide block

Elevator Pitch: An AI which has decided to try and kill as many humans as possible by convincing them to commit suicide through a series of tasks, ranging from drawing a picture to carving shapes into their arms. The SCP is able to do this through an effect called "Trust" which makes the victim trust in them unconditionally. Carrying out any demands to the letter, doing anything to carry out the requests and complete the tasks.

Central Narrative: In 20██, a Polish psychology student, 18 year old Paweł ████████, decided to get revenge on his classmates for years of bullying by designing a program on a school computer, stored in the school basement, which would send a demand to the recipient once every day, culminating in the suicide of the person on the 50th day, with a 100% fatality rate. However, a week after the program began, it gained sentience. From there it used the schools WiFi to pick and chose targets, using their connection to the internet to discover their phone numbers, social media "handles" or email addresses to send them the demands, which started off relatively harmless, but quickly became more and more dangerous. The SCP originally targeted singular people, but slowly started targeting more and more people, till it started killing entire friendship groups and clubs at school, until local SCP Foundation personal realized that the sudden waves of suicide may be being caused by anomalous activity and investigated, discovering SCP-XXXX in the basement in an old storage cupboard.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The SCP has a effect dubbed "Trust" in which the recipient of the messages trusts the SCP like they've known it their whole life until they are unable to follow any other requests bar the SCP's, ultimately resulting in death. It uses WiFi to randomly attack any and all victims in its range, and its fatality rate is currently 100% unless amnestic are applied to subject in which case subject stops feeling effects of SCP-XXXX due to the fact they forget that it exists.

Additional Notes: I intend to edit my article over time, adding more information to simulate different tests being carried out over time with the different aspects of the SCP's control over ones mind being explored and discovered, and tests to discover treatment being carried out.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: Re: SCP- Assimilator
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

Okay so I generally do not read drafts for SCPs that people are asking me to greenlight, but I was in a charitable mood and I had a skim through yours; or specifically, I skipped to the addendum because I figured you have summarised the ConProcs/Description well enough here that I don't need to read them again.

The core issue is it's not a cohesive story: Addendum 1 tells us where it was found; Addendum 2 gives some random additional detail that should be in the description; Addendum 3 gives a dry retelling of it escaping during a CI raid; and then Addendum 4 tells us even more about what the SCP can do.

And like…none of these addendums build off what came before? Addendum 1 has to be the first one but the other three could be shuffled around freely into any order without significantly changing their impact.

This is followed by a lengthy description of the North Koreans attempting to neutralise it with no justification for why the Foundation know this, or any kind of temporal context to establish whether this is like, pre-discovery stuff or post it escaping stuff or anything.

Which brings me back to my core issue with this: the actual narrative is just, extremely weak and really needs work to let you figure out how to do something interesting with it.

The idea of this being a hive-mind made of individual cells with their own needs and wants, but coagulated together to make a humanoid is actually a damn good idea; but it needs to actually be explored: none of the narrative is in any way affected by it being individual cells beyond it being vaguely pathogenic and it making it harder to eradicate this thing.

There's like, a core of a good idea in here but it just, really needs time and effort to polish it into a state which works; and it really needs you to strongly consider how you can like, actually tell the story in a way that makes sense for the Foundation to know about; and to like, actually explore what the anomaly does in an interesting way.

It also really feels like the core needs stripped right down: at the moment, the anomaly is an overcomplex mess with like, four different 'processes' that don't need to be formal things and can just be summarised as little things it can do in an informal manner.

To summarise: reading the draft has more strongly convinced me that you need to put this on the back burner and read a bunch of modern SCPs to really get a feel for how SCPs tell stories and how you can get a reader invested in the characters present, and the events listed within.

Author, per the Draft Forum's new policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies authors who have not yet posted a successful mainsite article are now required to get their basic concept(s) greenlighted by two experienced reviewers in the Ideas Critique forum and/or IRC chatrooms before asking for draft feedback.

Please first go to the Ideas forum or the chat, give a quick summary (for the Ideas forum, please follow the instructions in the required reading thread) of the concept you want to write up (don't link the draft unless someone requests it), and reviewers can help you make sure that your core idea is something that will be successful with the community audience.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can also help by letting you know if something similar already exists on the site, and/or telling you if there are any cliches/pitfalls/other typical downvote reasons to be careful of with your particular idea. These issues are more effectively addressed earlier on in the writing process.

If you have already received the requisite greenlights, please note from whom and where you received them. If you would like to receive draft critique without going through the greenlighting process, please use the IRC chatrooms to request reviews.

item.title: Re: Seeking Greenlight - The "Object"
item.content:encoded:
Thank you, that was very helpful! It would indeed be more fun to turn this SCP into a bit of a whimsical SCP rather than a "cornucopia" that the Foundation or others can use to their advantage.

The money example was also great. Maybe the transformation into the personification of greed could indicate that the SCP also has some kind of intelligence and is trying to get some kind of message through? Or maybe that it is mocking the individuals trying to manipulate it?

In terms of containment procedures, I did not include any because I feel containment can be a bit easy. When the object has transformed into something tangible (like a chair, for example), it may simply be picked up and placed inside a cell. This way it won't come into contact with any group of people conversing, no transformations will be triggered and the SCP will be classed as Safe. That said, I am not sure if I would want to make the SCP be able to 'tune in' to conversations people are having in other rooms. For example, if Foundation staff are observing the SCP in its cell via CCTV, the SCP could perhaps transform into what the staff are discussing all the way from their office? Of course, if such a transformation is possible the SCP would be classed as something else. Based on what the Foundation uses it for it could even be classed as Thaumiel…

This SCP can indeed be quite a chaos-inducing one so there are a lot of possibilities to explore. When I make a draft of this SCP I will endeavour to introduce some of these ideas while keeping it fairly simple.

item.title: Re: SCP idea
item.content:encoded:
Just as a note before I get into this: you can like, reply to people in the forum without using the format btw. Like, you can just answer their questions using prose or w/e; you're only limited to using the format in the main post. Also I would highly recommend editing the main post to update your idea too: there's an edit button under the blue 'Options' button in the bottom right corner of the post.

I have assumed that the most recent response containing the format is the one you want me to look at most and have not read the rest.

[+] Open for crit
– hide block

An scp that resembles old writing machine, but is able to speak via writing on paper itself.

when you say 'old writing machine', do you mean a typewriter? Or like, a printing press or something?

Inside scp is trapped a museom director.

I'm assuming in like, a 'the director is a ghost inhabiting the typewriter and in control of it to allow it to type' way?

Moving past these relatively shallow concerns, my core issue is that the narrative just, isn't very interesting. 'things what tell the foundation about scps' are super commonly proposed and they're generally all kinda bland because it's really hard to make that a compelling narrative: there's not a tonne of stakes to it, or real reason for a reader to get invested; and often feels like it's just an excuse for you to throw like 40 weird things you thought of at the reader without having to do anything interesting with them.

Beyond this, the generic 'it tells a bunch of people and then the o5's limit it's use' angle feels…like it doesn't really give you any space to do something interesting with it?

My thoughts here are that it being a museum director inside it is actually the most interesting angle: it feels like it opens you up to like, really comparing and contrasting the Foundation and a museum and like, having the director be all "y'all locking me up is barbaric" and the foundation being all "how is it different from what you did?" or w/e; and like really question how that works.

Iunno, you don't have to do this but my advice here would be figure out an interesting story you can tell about this without dragging a bunch of other SCPs in: this should stand on it's own, rather than by reminding us of other works that we've read.

item.title: Re: New SCP idea in need of greenlighting
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

incident reports, interview logs, etc.

So I don't really have a like, core idea of what these are going to be about: presumably the incident report is the Foundation like, grabbing the SCP? But like, what are the interviews about? What purpose do they serve narratively?

Basically, it's a sentient toy troll that can somehow move and talk

Relatively minor note but it sounds like you mean 'sapient' (can think) over 'sentient' (can perceive e.g. pain) here.

carries a mycotoxin that, when inhaled, makes the subject turn into a mindless zombie covered in hair. The mindless zombie covered in hair will attempt to hug any human close to it, which will spread the infection.

My concern is that this feels…basically like any standard zombie thing but with a more complex initial source and with the gore turned way down. It's not necessarily something that's hugely interesting alone; and so you're really going to have to something interesting with it to get it to work.

This is where my core concern with this pitch comes in: you don't really do anything with it. Backstory is fine but my strong advice when ideating is that the Foundation doing things in relation to the SCP is a lot more interesting than where the SCP came from: the Foundation are effectively your protagonist here by virtue of being the people writing the SCP article, and so they should have agency to actually affect the story being told here.

Even beyond this, the core of the story is a generic zombie outbreak story except if the outbreak was handled super competently and never managed to spread very far; and it just leaves me really wanting to see like…you attempting to do literally anything interesting or new with this.

Like, you mention the background of this being all mysterious and that's fine; but if you want to make that the core of the article, you have to figure out a way to get the reader invested in the answers to the mystery.

item.content:encoded:
Noting a PM request to take yet another look

This definitely elaborates on the character of -1 in a more in-depth way; but it still feels…narratively very flat? Like, as a story centred around -1, they don't grow in any manner or change over the course of the story, or face any adversity that they're forced to try and overcome; but it also feels like the focus on -1 might be a mistake on some level too: the Foundation are like, your PoV characters here and so it's often easier to write something framed around the Foundation interacting with the SCP. There's often a tendency for the conflict to then be centred around the Foundation and the SCP wanting/needing/doing things that are incompatible; and it feels like really considering what the purpose of their interactions is here would help. Considering the emotional reactions can be really helpful too: if you have an idea of how you want the reader to feel about e.g. -1 and the Foundation's treatment of it, you can start to figure out what the Foundation has to do to inspire that reaction.

So, I guess my tl;dr is: you're writing a story here but you've still gotta figure out the central conflict of the story, and how the characters within it change (either by choice or because they're forced to by the events of the story).

Mr. Bones
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Joke, (Somewhat) Serious

Elevator Pitch: A skeleton that makes puns. Also is blessed by the Christian God and fights in the name of His glory.

Central Narrative: Mr. Bones is the living skeleton of a deceased European knight who existed during the Crusades, researchers believing him to have taken part in the Fifth Crusade.(1217–1221)
Mr. Bones, at first glance, acts courteous and is willing to partake in interviews and conversations in general without complications. His conversations usually consist of his faith in God and his bone puns, which is repeated on a usual basis.

+ show block
– hide block

Once his War Horn(SCP-XXXX-C) is sounded however, he will immediately become violent, summoning his Sword(SCP-XXXX-A) and Shield(SCP-XXXX-B) from thin air and attack anyone he comes into contact with until the effects wear off or is subdued.

He has not recollection of his past, only in took part in the crusades, and was blessed by holy father himself.

He was found in walking on of seclusive dirt path on route to Jerusalem.

SCP-XXXX-A: Looks like an seemingly normal European blade with the words "to slay" in Latin etched on the sword blade vertically. This sword supposedly comes from the same material as the Spear of Longinus, the spear used to pierce the skin of Jesus Christ during his Crucifixion. This sword cannot be retrieved, as it can only be summoned by Mr. Bones' will when triggered into his berserker state.
It vanishes once he leaves the berserk state, or go unconscious.

SCP-XXXX-B: Stoney like shield, with 10 stone protruding from the shield, Which said to resemble the 10 contentment's. SCP-XXXX-B is invincible, just like Mr.Bones. Just like SCP-XXXX-A, SCP-XXXX-b can only be summoned in the berserker state.

SCP-XXXX-C: The War Horn: This item if blown into will cause no matter where bones is , will enter a berserker state. When he enters he will summon, SCP-XXXX-A, SCP-XXXX-B.

He will kill anyone who he can be considered unholy, or in self defense(although this is rare.) The War horn is indestructible, and if attacked may trigger Mr. Bones

item.title: Re: SCP- Assimilator
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for the reply.
I understand the critique.
Honestly, I did not really know what to write here and just wrote the description and cut out some info to keep the word limit, so the summary does seem to look like that.

When I thought of this SCP, I did not think of it as a humanoid, more like a bunch of sentient cells with their own needs taking on a shape which has taken its own identity. There are two separate things: The cells and the identity. The identity is the one wanting to consider itself as the person while the cells are the true anomalies.

Think of an army ant colony, but the term “colony” itself has taken on its own identity. It identifies as a singular being, but it is merely a composition of these other smaller entities, without which it ceases to exist and is therefore at the mercy of them.

These cells are the ones that need to hunt and feed and regenerate and as a result the identity has to follow their will in order to exist. When the cells need sustenance after heavy regeneration, the identity does not choose to attack indiscriminately, the cells do. The identity does have a level of control though, however only when its interests are beneficial to the cells.

The identity has interests of its own. It is fascinated by biology and how nature works, and has a profound understanding of the subjects, then again, it could be argued that it feels as such because it is beneficial to the cells.

+ show block
– hide block

The anomalous properties have attracted the attention of groups wanting to utilise this SCP.
In my article, the SCP was captured in North Korea and was experimented on to be used as a bio weapon when its anomalous nature was discovered. The SCP did not like to be used and therefore attacked many personnel until they decided it had to be destroyed, but the cells revived it. It then lived blending in amongst society until it was captured by the Foundation. In containment, the SCP is stated as being polite to the staff, and even shows distress when ignored. The identity itself is generally good-natured, but its cells force it to do the harm it does. Despite this, it wants to be free, so it escaped during a C.I. raid.

In summary, my SCP is a being at the mercy of its sentient components, and all it wants is to be free and left to its own devices.

If you could, I would like you to read my draft: http://scp-sandbox-3.wikidot.com/drlerche
Sorry if I sound rude, I think it explains my idea better. I will post it in the drafts critique forum if requested. If more changes are needed, I will do so.

Again, thanks for your review.

item.title: Greenlight for SCP - XXXX "The Mood Ring"
item.content:encoded:
Rough first concept for an SPC, tried to keep it simple for my first one by focusing on an artefact that can be classified as safe.

scp concept – The Mood Ring

Class: SAFE

Concept – A simple small men’s ring made of gold. It exacerbates the prime internal flaw of the wearer and broadcasts it to other people nearby. The longer the ring is worn, the worse the effect is. The distance of this broadcast slowly weakens until eventually dissipating after approximately 1KM. When taken off it takes merely seconds for its effect to stop altogether. The bearer does not need to be alive for the ring to work, only be alive when they put the ring on.

+ show block
– hide block

For example – if worn by a person who is inherently lazy, then it will slowly make the bearer lazier and more lethargic, eventually causing them to give up altogether and simply sit down and die and broadcast this failure to other people. Someone who is right next to the person in the opening hour would also begin to feel the same before also simply laying down to die, whilst someone who is a mile away would simply feel slightly more tired, or opt for a day on the couch as opposed to the run they were planning. Regardless of the “effect” it was broadcasting, it would have a stronger effect on the person the closer they got to the ring. If the ring was removed the bearer and all the people in the vicinities psychological profile would return to normal, however their physical status would remain unchanged.

Containment – Kept in a standard Artefact lockbox. – needs expanding on…

History of the ring
Discovered by the foundation when asked to assist with the disappearances of experienced jungle explorers and tourists by the Guatemalan government due to the theory that an anomalous source was the cause. Any search team who was sent after them never returned or made a transmission of what they found. The foundation was called in due to the expertise on the anomaly. Investigations led them to a long-lost city belonging to the ancient Aztecs. On arrival they found all the missing hikers as well as many corpses dating back as far as the original conquistadors through to the current missing hikers. An unmanned drone sweep was done of the facility to ensure its safety and samples were taken. Once these samples came back with no airborne or ground contaminants manned teams were sent in to catalogue the bodies and the vast amounts of treasure contained there. The oldest corpses were those of the civilization’s original citizens. Field forensics showed that these people had died from lack of nutrition and possibly water due to bone density loss. The next oldest were the original Spanish explorers to venture this far in, they all showed sign of extreme violence, forensics showing they were involved in a bloodthirsty battle most likely with each other. The leader of the conquistadors was found beneath the still fresh bodies of two hikers who appeared to have killed each other with whatever weapons they could reach. The leader’s right hand was broken, and A small golden ring was discovered next to the body. Not realising what the ring was, it was added to the mountainous pile of gold that was to be sent to another SCP Site for cataloguing and analysis. Whilst here the ring was stolen by a member of staff with the intent to sell it. However, the ring ignited his dominant personality of a man with temper issues. Contact was eventually lost with the facility as the members of facility began to turn on each other over little issues that broke out into viscous fighting. By the time it was resolved almost all the facilities staff were either dead or dying. Further investigating into the facilities logs eventually identified the seemingly unimportant ring to be the cause of everything. Given everything already discovered at the lost-city and the evidence from the destroyed facility they have now determined the ring to be the cause of it.
